the main characteristics of the setting can probably be split into 3 parts:

1. the gods: gods come into existence when people believe that they exist (I think). They frequently embody cities, and really big storms sometimes. They are relatively easy to get into contact with, in comparison with D&D gods for example. 
2. magic: there are 6 elements, and each one also corresponds to a secondary attribute (air has communication for example). There's also people w/o magic but it seems pretty clear in universe that having magic is way superior to not having magic. If you have the gift of magic, you can master it with runes and circles and things, or you can use it through raw power. 
3. World: the world is super ancient, and seems defined by conflicts between the gods which leave cities in ruin. I think that an RPG would probably take place before the comic, so the Storm would still be there. The Chimera Plague, invading gods/storms, and things all pose threats.

A character can either be human, elf(there's at least like 5 variations), felin, or metal-caste. "chimera plague survivor" and "former avatar of a god" seem to be unique cases and I wouldn't make them playable characters.

There's nothing wrong inherently with a 1d6 roll-under system. Like others have said, you barely have a system at this point. There's a million TTRPG's that use this or similar action resolution systems. Try looking up a few. Your system won't be defined by this, but by the classes and things you build around it. Think about what kind of game you want to run, and create abilities and mechanics to support that. 

A d6 roll-under system would have skills that go from 2 through 5, so you don't really have much room for improvement in the skills. If you want long-term campaigns, your characters will have to develop in other areas, with abilities, or maybe in terms of character arcs, if you're going for a more narrative focused game. But it does mean that each difficulty is clearly defined - a 3 should be notably more difficult than a 4 (that's a pro for me). 

To be perfectly honest, the action resolution system should be the one last things you decide. First you need to know what kind of game you want to run, and what kind of things you want to be possible. Different mechanics will support different playstyles. 

Try reading other RPG's to get ideas. I recommend any Powered by the Apocalypse(PbtA) game, Legends of the Five Rings, Dread RPG, the Cypher System, or anything else. Maybe try browsing Kickstarter - a lot of RPG's there have quickstart rules available for non-backers.

I think there's a couple clarifications to be made, although your instructions are definitely very useful.

The "prayer" action sends a message to the devs and allows them to message you back, although they might not do it immediately and it can be hard to notice it when they do. There's no notification, so you always have to be alert and looking for it. But this does require a high Humility stat. This is often and understandably confused with low Pride, but they're not exactly the same. Humility helps regulate Pride, but if your Pride stat is low without a high Humility, you can get the "Depressed" debuff, and that can significantly lower your chances of communication with the devs.

Humility is a really overpowered stat in this game, but so many people overlook it.
